requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

task.description: Validate test/specs/REQ-124.md and the two test files (test/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config_test.exs, test/letflow/identity_test.exs's new safe_get_tenant_by_slug/2 describe block) independently, per WF-02 Step 3b's standard procedure. Read the test spec and source files directly -- do not read TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary as a substitute. Give particular attention to: (1) the exact-shape test really does a sorted-key-set equality assertion, not a subset/pattern match. (2) the unknown-slug/missing-slug/nil-realm-id branches are asserted BYTE-IDENTICAL (plain map equality), not merely 'both 200'. (3) the pipeline-wide-vs-route-specific auth test actually calls a real ApiPipeline-mounted route with no Authorization header and asserts 401. (4) fixtures are per-test unique, no shared hardcoded tenant slugs that could collide across tests or with other suites. (5) TEST-DESIGNER flagged one discrepancy in its handoff -- the dispatch named test/letflow/routers/tenant_config_test.exs as a reference file that doesn't exist, and TEST-DESIGNER used test/letflow/routers/req078_supporting_routes_test.exs's actual dispatch style instead. Confirm that substitution was reasonable and the resulting test style is still consistent with the codebase's established router-test pattern.
acceptance_criteria: At least one runnable test targets each of the five acceptance criteria listed below -- no @tag :skip without a passing counterpart
No 'TODO: implement test' left in either spec or test file
Test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution
Tests are self-sufficient -- don't depend on other tests running first
No hardcoded secrets/connection strings in test files
GET /tenant-config [/api/mobile/tenant-config] returns the five specified fields for a known tenant slug with no Authorization header, demonstrated by a test that sends no token
a test asserts that the endpoint exposes no field beyond the five specified -- an exact-shape assertion (sorted key-set equality), not a subset check
the behaviour for an unknown tenant slug is tested and shown byte-identical to the default/missing-slug branch
every other route under Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline still requires authentication, proven by a test that would fail if the exemption were pipeline-wide
